text.p: Optical Coating Laboratory Inc Thursday said it expects gradual quarter-to-quarter improvement for the balance of fiscal 1997.

In a statement accompanying its first quarter financial results, Optical Coating attributed the improved outlook to its continued focus on initiatives to improve manufacturing yields and cycle time, in combination with several new product introductions.
The Santa Rosa, Calif.-based manufacturer of optical thin film coated components earned $667,000 or $0.07 a share in the first quarter ended January 31.
In the same period last year, the company earned a profit of $500,000 or $0.05 a share.

"We are continuing to see improvements in throughput and yield in our new continuous coater platform," said Chairman Herb Dwight. "These improvements, combined with continued strong performance in our precision coating operations, had a significant positive impact on the company's domestic income from operations in the first quarter of 1997."
However, he said first quarter results continued to be affected by the operating results of its German subsidiary which is experiencing weak demand for its office automation products.

"We have taken steps to lower our cost structure, including a previously announced 15 percent workforce reduction," Dwight said. "The workforce reduction occurred during the first quarter and is expected to have a positive impact on future quarters."
